name: Primary Cutaneous B-Cell Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of solitary or multiple skin lesions without extracutaneous involvement at diagnosis
Histological confirmation of B-cell lymphoma with characteristic immunophenotype (CD20+, CD79a+)
Immunohistochemical profile consistent with B-cell lineage and exclusion of systemic lymphoma
Absence of nodal or visceral involvement confirmed by imaging and bone marrow biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of B-cell lymphoma in skin lesions without evidence of extracutaneous disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of systemic B-cell lymphoma and confirmation of primary cutaneous origin.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Solitary or clustered erythematous to violaceous cutaneous nodules or plaques
searchTerms: single or grouped red to purple skin nodules or plaques
clustered erythematous to violaceous skin lumps

pathognomonic.symptomName: Indolent, slowly enlarging skin tumors localized primarily on the head, neck, or trunk
searchTerms: slowly growing skin tumors on head, neck, or trunk
indolent skin growths enlarging over time
skin tumors with gradual enlargement in central body areas

common.symptomName: Localized pruritus over affected skin areas

occasional.symptomName: Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever

occasional.symptomName: Pain or tenderness localized to skin lesions

rare.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
searchTerms: general body symptoms like fever and sweating

laboratory: Histopathology showing dense dermal infiltrate of atypical B-cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, CD79a, BCL-2, and variable BCL-6
Normal peripheral blood counts in most cases
imaging: PET-CT or CT scan showing absence of extracutaneous disease
Ultrasound of regional lymph nodes to exclude systemic involvement
genetic: Frequent t(14;18)(q32;q21) translocation involving BCL2 gene in follicle center lymphoma subtype
Somatic mutations in MYD88 in some cases
other: Bone marrow biopsy negative for lymphoma infiltration
Flow cytometry confirming monoclonal B-cell population in skin lesions

distinguishingFeatures: Different clinical presentation with patches and plaques rather than nodules
Presence of systemic lymphadenopathy or organ involvement
Positive bone marrow or peripheral blood involvement

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging or ulcerating skin lesions
Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Evidence of extracutaneous dissemination on imaging or biopsy
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Pileri SA, et al. The 2016 revision of the World Health Organization classification of lymphoid neoplasms. Blood. 2016.
Grange F, Beylot-Barry M. Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphomas: an update. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2016.
